source.inspection: The completed pinned source analysis identified four async states and promise-driven outcomes as useful mechanisms. No upstream source, assets, package or Motion dependency were copied.

adoptedMechanisms: Keep one action control across idle, pending, success and error states.
Derive the visible result from the supplied asynchronous Promise outcome.
originalChanges: Implement original Product Craft React, CSS and portable HTML; no upstream implementation or visual asset is reused.
Use a Promise<void> contract: only resolution becomes success; rejection or a synchronous throw becomes a persistent retry state.
Guard duplicate activation, keep keyboard focus on the native control while pending and ignore stale settlement after unmount.
Give each instance its own status-description ID and isolate observer callbacks from the action's Promise outcome.
Use a 46px target, Product Craft palette and shape, and a reduced-motion mode with no transition or spinner rotation.
Keep the fictional fixture explicit: the Promise never writes files, accounts, projects, invoices or service data.
baseline: Interactive plain Save changes action in the same fictional Wren Studio Launch note. It reports activation only and has no simulated save state; the baseline is not a screenshot of an existing product.

portableArtifact.status: Approved artifact replaced in the same Library item; current version 1 confirmed by read

usageApi.onSave: Required callback returning Promise<void>; resolve only after the actual operation succeeds and reject on failure.
usageApi.successMessage: Optional confirmation shown only after Promise resolution.
usageApi.errorMessage: Optional persistent, actionable error copy shown after rejection or synchronous throw.
usageApi.onStateChange: Optional observer notified for pending, success and error transitions only; the initial idle state is not emitted. Observer errors must not alter the action outcome or block completion.
usageApi.reset: Success remains terminal for the mounted instance. Remount with a new React key to begin a new action; the demo's Reset simulation control uses this contract.
usageApi.cancellation: The caller owns cancellation of its operation. Ignoring settlement after unmount prevents stale UI updates and does not cancel a request or undo an action.
usageApi.storyOnly: The Promise fixture, comparison baseline, fictional content, retry scenario and reset control belong to the demonstration, not a live product integration.

demoBoundaries: Both samples are fictional; no financial, invoice, file, account, project or product service is connected.
The success label says Resolved and the live message says that nothing was written.
The baseline confirms activation only and never claims that a save occurred.

verification.browserRendered: Approved Components / Buttons catalog and the standalone approved HTML rendered in installed Chrome. Desktop catalog screenshot inspected; heading, sample, usage and provenance remain readable.
verification.browserKeyboard: Tab reached the action with a visible 3px focus outline. Space and Enter activated the local fixtures; rejection persisted, Space retry resolved, and focus remained on the button. Repeated pending activation remained one attempt.
verification.browserPromiseStates: Resolved fixture showed Resolved only after its Promise settled. Reject-once fixture exposed a persistent Retry save state, then a second Space activation resolved successfully.
verification.browserMobile: At 390 CSS px, document width was 390 and component width 366. At requested 320 CSS px, Chrome reported effective innerWidth/document width 322 and component width 296; the control fit. The portable HTML also fit its requested 320px emulation. This is emulation, not a physical-device session.
verification.browserReducedMotion: In the catalog and portable HTML, prefers-reduced-motion emulation yielded transition-duration 0s and spinner animation-name none while result labels remained available.
verification.browserPageErrors: Zero runtime exceptions in the final fresh-page pass. Six intentional observer exceptions were caught and logged during the observer-isolation test.
verification.workflowTests: Passed: all 44 workflow tests, including six Morph Status fixture, accessible-instance, route, portable and approval cases
verification.physicalDeviceScreenReader: Not tested; physical device, screen reader, assistive technology and zoom sessions remain outside this verification.
verification.browserReuse: Two mounted reusable controls had unique status-description IDs and independent outcomes. Duplicate activation called onSave once; rejection then retry called it twice. Throwing observers during pending/success/error did not alter Promise resolution, rejection or synchronous-throw outcomes. Late resolve and reject after unmount emitted no terminal observer notification.
